annotation.evidence_span: An origin server can apply any normalization method, whereas other servers MUST perform scheme-based normalization
annotation.interpretation_a: Origin servers are free to use any normalization method, potentially leading to inconsistencies in how requests are processed across different servers. Other servers are constrained to scheme-based normalization.
annotation.interpretation_b: The statement implies a distinction between 'origin servers' and 'other servers' but doesn't define what constitutes 'other servers'. This could include proxies, caches, or load balancers. The lack of a clear definition creates ambiguity about which servers are subject to the scheme-based normalization requirement.
annotation.justification: The clause creates ambiguity because it doesn't define 'other servers'. This leaves room for different interpretations of which servers are required to perform scheme-based normalization, potentially leading to inconsistent behavior.
annotation.missing_information: A clear definition of 'other servers' is needed to determine the scope of the MUST requirement. Without it, implementations may differ on which servers must perform scheme-based normalization.
